_comment: Observed pass records, and the only evidence gate_liveness.py accepts.
Written by tools/gate_liveness_record.py at the END of a job that
reached it -- reachable only when that job's steps passed. The liveness
tool READS this and never writes it: a gate asserting it works is the
mistake the tool exists to catch, so the two must not be the same file.
A test's record carries `via` naming the job that ran the suite. The
suite passing is evidence for each test it collected; the field says so
rather than implying the test was invoked on its own.

Records whose run is `local` were verified on a machine, not a runner, and say so. They are replaced by a real run id the first time CI collects the suite, which is the mechanism keeping this log honest -- and a record that claimed a runner it did not have would be the defect this tool exists to catch.

This file is a SNAPSHOT. The recorder writes it inside a runner's checkout, which is discarded when the job ends, so nothing commits it and no run refreshes it for you. Each CI run appends the delta it produced to the job's step summary instead, and a person commits those records when they want the snapshot to move. A gate with no record here is reported NEVER_PASSED, which is the honest answer: nothing has been observed.
